To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Zika virus (ZikV) induces small RNAs in Aedes aepgpti cells that are loaded into the Ago2 and Ago3 exo-siRNAS and piRNA pathways respectively.
ZIKV infection of Aedes cells induces exo-siRNAs, but not piRNAs, which are loaded onto Ago2, but not Ago3, Piw5 or Piw6.

ZIKV infection of Ae. aegyptii cells results in the production of exo-siRNAs, but not piRNAs, that are associated with Ago2 and that the production of exogenous siRNAs is required for the control of ZIKV in Ae. aegptii cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the ZIKV induced small RNA response and its role in the antivirals response of A. aegyptivector cells.
the identification of mosquito RNAi components that are involved in ZIKV replication.
the characterization of the RNAi response to ZIKV in Ae. aegyptii cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZIKV does not induce an antiviral response in the exo-sRNA pathway in A. aegyptin cells.
ZIKV is not inhibited by RNAi in mosquito cells.
ZIKV does not inhibit exo-siRNAs, and the exo-sRNAi pathway is not involved in the antivial response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ZIKV does not inhibit exo-siRNAs but it does inhibit PIWI4.

ZIKV infection in Aedes aedes aegytpi-derived cells induces the production of virus-specific siRNAs that are loaded into the exogenous siRNA pathway effector Ago2, which is the key mosquito ant-viral response pathway.
Zika virus infection in Aedes aeygpti cells induces a robust antiviral RNAi response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ZIKV infection in A. aegypt i cells is not inhibited by RNAi and that ZIKV C protein is not an exogenous siRNA pathway inhibitor.
ZIKV infection in mosquito cells does not induce the exo-sRNA pathway, but rather induces a noncanonical piRNA pathway.
the exo siRNA pathway is involved in the antivirals response to ZIKV in mosquito cells.
